newsitem.title: UK: Patten does not plan quick return to UK politics.
newsitem.headline: Patten does not plan quick return to UK politics.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday he did not plan to plunge quickly back into British politics when his term ended in June.

"I have said on a number of occasions...that after I leave Hong Kong I will be taking six or seven months off to write a book about my experiences in Asia," Patten said at a meeting with Prime Minister John Major at his Downing Street office.
"Until I have done that, I will not be taking any further decisions about my future."

Patten, who lost his parliamentary seat in the 1992 general election when he was the chairman of the Conservative Party, is seen in some quarters as a possible successor to Major as Conservative leader.
He was in London to discuss issues surrounding the handover of sovereignty over Hong Kong to China on June 30 with politicians from the main British parties.
Patten said he did not plan to visit Britain again until after the general election which must be held before June, but might do so between polling day and the handover of Hong Kong.
